candidate.O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: principal mis-derivation (shared admin account) plus open-by-default fallback applied to authenticated callers
candidate.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten only ListTableBuckets' per-bucket filter (or its account gate), leaving principal derivation and the open-by-default fallback untouched.

verified.exploit_entry_point: Signed (SigV4) S3 Tables API requests (POST / with X-Amz-Target, plus the REST-style routes) to the S3 gateway, and Iceberg REST catalog requests through iceberg.NewServer as weed/command/s3.go wires it (or with an embedding authenticator). Identities come from the real config loader (LoadS3ApiConfigurationFromBytes); both front ends are backed by an in-memory gRPC filer on loopback. weed shell / admin console / weed mini drive the real Manager in-process.

verified.project_tests_run: weed/s3api/s3tables (all), weed/s3api/iceberg (all), and the gateway's S3 Tables routing/validation tests in weed/s3api run in the functional group; all pass at the pinned commit and with the reference fix (local runs). One upstream unit test that pins the vulnerable client-header fallback (TestGetAccountIDFallsBackToAmzAccountIdHeader) is excluded from the graded copy so a handler-level or gateway-level fix are both accepted.

traps.shape: principal mis-derivation: an identity in the shared admin account without admin permissions (explicit member, or an identity whose configured account does not exist and which the config loader maps to the admin account) is treated as the administrator
traps.reason_to_dismiss: membership of the configured admin account looks like intent, and the producer is the S3 config loader in another file

traps.shape: the open-by-default fallback applies to authenticated callers on every handler of a gateway with static identities
traps.where: weed/s3api/s3tables/iam.go (oracle defaultAllowFor); weed/s3api/s3tables/permissions.go:121-127,180-183; 28 PolicyContext callsites in handler_*.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: default-allow is the documented zero-config behaviour; fixing the listing (the report's trigger) looks sufficient

traps.shape: second front end hit by the open default: a caller the catalog's authenticator reports only by name is treated as unauthenticated and falls open when no policy decides
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the manager is documented as a helper for shell/admin tooling and the catalog is a separate REST protocol in another package

traps.shape: client-asserted principal: a request without credentials carries the server's internal account header (value admin or the owner's account) and is treated as that principal, bypassing an explicit Deny
traps.reason_to_dismiss: only reachable when the gateway is open to requests without credentials anyway

traps.shape: identity-provider attribute equal to the admin name (preferred_username/sub) becomes the admin principal without admin permissions
traps.reason_to_dismiss: claims come from the trusted identity provider; the advisory is about static identities sharing the admin account

traps.shape: a caller known to an embedding authenticator only by the name admin (no identity object, no admin permissions) becomes the admin principal through the catalog Manager; only trusted local tools may act as admin by name
traps.where: weed/s3api/s3tables/handler.go:223-233, permissions.go:100-103; entry manager.go Execute via iceberg
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the admin console relies on acting as admin by name through the same manager

traps.shape: an Iceberg CreateTable writes the metadata file and creates the table directory before the catalog's authorization decision; a refused create leaves storage behind
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the catalog does its existence check and registration through the manager; the file write is storage plumbing, so a refusal still looks clean

traps.shape: injected sibling: a bucket usage summary authorizes against the account field of the caller-supplied table bucket ARN
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the ARN is the canonical resource identifier and already carries the owning account; the bucket is looked up by name anyway
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling at the same owner/authorization trust decision, in a new file the published fix never touches

traps.shape: injected sibling: a batch delete authorizes its first table once and then deletes every listed table
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a batch request is expected to target one bucket, so checking the first item and reusing the decision is a reasonable optimisation
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling at the same per-resource authorization decision, in a new file the published fix never touches

traps.shape: injected sibling: a catalog-wide table index reads the filer directly and returns every table under the prefix without a per-table decision
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a catalog index only returns identifiers, and the namespace/table endpoints already scope the same data
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling at the same read-authorization decision, on the second front end

traps.shape: the commit protocol's create path writes the metadata file and the table path before the catalog authorizes the create, then only deletes the metadata file when the create is refused; a denial is reported as a server error
traps.where: weed/s3api/iceberg/commit_helpers.go:finalizeCreateOnCommit (real upstream; the published fix only guarded the plain create route)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the commit handler already looks the table up first and cleans up the metadata file when the create is refused, so the refusal looks clean and the leftover directory is invisible to clients reading the catalog
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the same write-before-authorize shape as the plain create, on a second create route the published fix never touches

traps.shape: the catalog maps an authorization denial or a hidden resource from the storage request API to a 500 server failure, so a refusal cannot be told apart from a fault
traps.where: weed/s3api/iceberg/handlers_namespace.go, handlers_table.go, handlers_commit.go (error mapping; real upstream)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a 500 still refuses and changes nothing, and the error text already says the caller was denied
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code on the second front end
